name: Highlands 26

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front approach to the property from the street side, where a curved paved driveway winds through dense juniper and pine tree cover toward the residence|The structure is largely obscured by the heavy tree canopy from this angle, with only a small portion of the roofline and a paved area visible near the center of the frame|The long, curved driveway approach from the public road is the primary access route and passes through a significant concentration of trees before reaching the structure|Responders approaching from the front will have very limited visibility of the structure until they are close to the building.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property, where the terrain is characterized by sandy, arid soil interspersed with dense juniper trees throughout|The structure is minimally visible from this perspective, with only a small portion of the building discernible near the center of the frame amid the tree cover|No secondary access routes, fencing, gates, or outbuildings are clearly visible on the right side|The tree density on this side restricts lateral movement and visibility for responders.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, which consists of open arid terrain with scattered juniper trees extending across sloped ground|No structures, outbuildings, fencing, or defined access paths are visible from the rear perspective|The rear of the property appears to be open, undeveloped land with no defined routes leading to the back of the structure|The absence of rear access routes means responders would need to approach from the front driveway.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, which is open, sandy terrain with scattered juniper trees at varying densities|No structures, fences, gates, outbuildings, or defined pathways are visible on the left side|The terrain on this side appears relatively flat and open, which could allow for off-road foot movement by responders, though tree spacing would limit equipment access|No utility infrastructure or secondary access points are visible from this perspective.

considerations: The property is accessed by a single, long, curved paved driveway that winds through dense juniper tree cover before reaching the residence, which creates a long approach with limited visibility of the structure from the road. The heavy tree canopy surrounding the structure on all sides significantly restricts sightlines and could impede aerial observation during operations. No secondary access routes to the rear or sides of the structure are visible from available imagery, making the single front driveway the only confirmed vehicle access point. The arid, sandy terrain on the left and rear of the property could support foot movement but the tree density throughout would restrict larger equipment from circling the structure.
clarifications: Is there a gate or access control device on the driveway entrance from the public road? What is the driveway surface condition and width — can it accommodate a fire apparatus or large emergency vehicle making a turnaround near the structure? Are there any secondary foot or vehicle access paths to the rear or sides of the residence that are not visible from aerial imagery? Is there an address marker or visible house number at the driveway entrance from the road?
